step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-input CMOS NAND gate input-skew characterization circuit
step1_figure.description: Two 2-input CMOS NAND gates with swapped NMOS stack positions used to simulate and compare the propagation delays of toggling the bottom NMOS transistor (input A with B high, output outa) versus the top NMOS transistor (input B with A high, output outb).

tPHL_A.description: High-to-low propagation delay of Outa when toggling the bottom NMOS device (input A) while the top NMOS device is already ON (B held high at VDD)

equation.explanation: High-to-low propagation delay through the two series NMOS pull-down transistors. When switching the bottom NMOS, the internal node N001 starts precharged near VDD - Vthn, but discharging proceeds quickly as both channels conduct, resulting in the faster delay outa.
equation.assumptions: Linear RC approximation of MOSFET digital resistance; step/ramp input with finite rise time tr_in

sky130_expected.calculation: With Wn/Ln = 2.0u/0.15u = 13.33, un*Cox = 270 uA/V^2, VDD = 1.8V, Vthn = 0.42V: ID,sat = 0.5 * 270u * 13.33 * (1.8 - 0.42)^2 = 3.43 mA. Effective digital resistance Rn ≈ VDD / ID,sat ≈ 525 ohms. Total pull-down resistance R_eff = Rn1 + Rn4 ≈ 1050 ohms. Intrinsic RC delay = 0.7 * 1050 * 50fF ≈ 36.8 ps. Adding input transition contribution (0.5 * 100ps = 50ps) gives tPHL_A ≈ 87 ps to 150 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite input rise time (100 ps) and body effect on the upper series NMOS increase effective delay beyond ideal RC.

tPHL_B.description: High-to-low propagation delay of Outb when toggling the top NMOS device while the bottom NMOS device is already ON (B held high at VDD)

equation.explanation: High-to-low propagation delay when the top NMOS device is switched. Because the top transistor experiences body effect and its source is initially elevated until the stack conducts, it turns on slightly later, resulting in outb being slower than outa.
equation.assumptions: Linear RC approximation of series NMOS with intermediate node parasitic and body effect

sky130_expected.calculation: Using similar parameters (R_eff ≈ 1050 ohms, Cload = 50 fF), but with top NMOS experiencing transient body effect and Vgs reduction during the turn-on transition, adding ~20-50 ps of delay: tPHL_B ≈ tPHL_A + 30 ps ≈ 150 ps to 280 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Top transistor switching experiences reduced overdrive during early transient due to intermediate node potential.

skew_tPHL.description: Input-dependent propagation delay skew between toggling the two different inputs of the NAND gate

equation.explanation: The difference in propagation delays between the top and bottom input paths of the NAND gate, directly illustrating the input-dependent skew discussed on page 533.
equation.assumptions: Identical capacitive load (50 fF) and identical input transition time on both gates

sky130_expected.calculation: In Fig 18.15, the delay skew is approximately 50-100 ps for short-channel devices. In SKY130 (0.15um length, VDD=1.8V), skew_tPHL = tPHL_B - tPHL_A ≈ 20 ps to 50 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Skew arises strictly from the asymmetric position of NMOS transistors in the series pull-down stack.

fall_time_outa.description: Fall time (90% to 10% of VDD, 1.62 V to 0.18 V) of output Outa

equation.explanation: 10% to 90% fall time for a step-driven RC network discharging through two series NMOS transistors.
equation.assumptions: Standard CMOS logic 10%-90% fall time formula

sky130_expected.reasoning: Discharge through 2 series NMOS transistors of W/L = 2u/0.15u into 50 fF.

fall_time_outb.description: Fall time (90% to 10% of VDD, 1.62 V to 0.18 V) of output Outb

equation.explanation: 10% to 90% fall time of Outb when discharged through the series NMOS stack.
equation.assumptions: Standard CMOS logic 10%-90% fall time formula

sky130_expected.calculation: Similar discharge resistance once both transistors are fully on: t_fall ≈ 2.2 * 1050 * 50e-15 ≈ 120 ps to 160 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Once channels are conducting, fall transition slope matches closely with Outa.

step3_testbench.description: Transient simulation testbench replicating Fig 18.15 to measure tPHL of Outa and Outb, the propagation delay skew between inputs, and fall times.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Fig 18.15 Skew in Logic Gates - NAND Gate Input Delay Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Sizing parameters
.param W_xm1=2.0u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=2.0u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=2.0u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=2.0u L_xm4=0.15u
.param W_xm5=2.0u L_xm5=0.15u
.param W_xm6=2.0u L_xm6=0.15u
.param W_xm7=2.0u L_xm7=0.15u
.param W_xm8=2.0u L_xm8=0.15u

* DUT Netlist from prompt
xm1 N001 A 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2 Outa A VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm3 Outa B VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 Outa B N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm5 N002 B 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm6 Outb B VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
xm7 Outb A VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
xm8 Outb A N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
VB B 0 1.8
C1 Outa 0 5e-14
C2 Outb 0 5e-14

* Input stimulus: step pulse on A starting at 0.5ns with 100ps rise time
VA A 0 pulse(0 1.8 0.5n 100p 100p 2n 4n)

* Control script
.control
tran 10p 1.5n 0 10p

* Propagation delays from 50% Vin (0.9V) to 50% Vout (0.9V)
meas tran tPHL_A trig v(A) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Outa) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran tPHL_B trig v(A) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Outb) val=0.9 fall=1

* Input-dependent skew
let skew_tPHL = tPHL_B - tPHL_A
print tPHL_A tPHL_B skew_tPHL

* Fall times (90% to 10% of 1.8V -> 1.62V to 0.18V)
meas tran fall_time_outa trig v(Outa) val=1.62 fall=1 targ v(Outa) val=0.18 fall=1
meas tran fall_time_outb trig v(Outb) val=1.62 fall=1 targ v(Outb) val=0.18 fall=1
print fall_time_outa fall_time_outb

quit
.endc
.end
